chunks: And from him, from Ali, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Abu Ayyub, who said:
I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): 'What is the minimum distance at which the traveler shortens his prayer?' He said, 'Barid.'

key_terms.بَرِيدٌ: Barid (a unit of distance, approx. 4 farsakhs or 22-24 km)

ai.seo_question: What is the minimum distance for a traveler to shorten their prayers according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) defines the minimum travel distance for shortening prayers as 'Barid', a classical unit of measurement. This establishes the jurisprudential baseline for the concession of *Qasr*, reflecting the practical ease (*Raf' al-Haraj*) granted to travelers in Shia fiqh. The specification of a concrete distance underscores the importance of clear boundaries in ritual obligations.
